clue.text: Leader of boys' gang demands, loudly, a drink

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical direction to play loudly
gin is a spirit, a strong drink

explanation.surface: The boss of a youth gang loudly orders a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demands' is only a link here: the leader 'demands' (needs) the pieces that follow. Fagin leads the gang of boy pickpockets in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: In Oliver Twist the old fence trains and runs a gang of young London pickpockets.

clue.text: These eggs? Put 13 on the cooker

parts.note: the answer to 13 down means unhindered, which is free
a range is an old-fashioned kitchen stove

explanation.surface: A cook is told to put a certain answer on the stove when making eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' just means placed above. The cross-reference 13 is to 13 down, meaning unhindered.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs laid by hens allowed to roam outdoors are sold under this label.

clue.text: So playful a goat not so sure-footed?

explanation.surface: A goat so frisky it keeps stumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing the giddy goat' is a British idiom for fooling around.
explanation.definitionFit: Frivolous, as in playing the goat; also dizzy and unsteady on one's feet.

clue.text: After prison rising in France she takes car in flight

indicators.note: after places the French word behind the turned-round prison word
in a down clue rising means the word for prison is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: can is slang for prison
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: Released from jail, a Frenchwoman catches a plane in her car.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads the word upwards. The 'car' is the gondola hung beneath an airship or balloon, not a motor car.
explanation.definitionFit: The basket or gondola of a balloon or airship, later the housing for an aircraft engine.

clue.text: Nothing unusually posh in a voyage in this

indicators.note: the word in tells us these letters go inside the voyage word

parts.note: a trip is a voyage or journey
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of posh appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A traveller notes there is nothing very smart about this sea journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'this', pointing back to the vessel the whole clue describes; 'unusually' anagrams posh before the lot goes 'in' the voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel for carrying soldiers is the kind of ship one would make such a voyage in.

clue.text: A three-foot seat for one that worked the oracle

definitions.text: A three-foot seat for one that worked the oracle

parts.words: A three-foot seat for one that worked the oracle
parts.note: the priestess at Delphi sat on a three-legged stool to prophesy

explanation.surface: A three-legged chair used by a fortune-teller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-foot' means three-legged, not a yard high. The Pythia, Apollo's priestess at Delphi, delivered prophecies seated on one.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged stand, like the stool of the Delphic priestess.

clue.text: It's without prejudice, Sir William (RA) has no right to object

indicators.note: has no tells us a letter is removed from the painter's surname

parts.note: Sir William Orpen was an Irish portrait painter and Royal Academician
to mind something is to object to it

explanation.surface: A painter claims impartiality but is not entitled to complain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' takes R from ORPEN, leaving OPEN. 'Without prejudice' is a legal phrase, but here it describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptive attitude free of bias or preconceptions.

clue.text: For women, is sleep a sort of cover-up?

indicators.note: a sort of suggests the letters of is sleep form a version of something else

explanation.surface: Is sleep a kind of disguise for women?
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' rearranges IS SLEEP. 'For women' adds that this was a lady's garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A long fur-lined cloak or mantle once worn by women, a garment that covers one.

clue.text: Physicist hard to bear, being on this we hear?

indicators.note: we hear tells us the answer sounds like the phrase described

parts.words: hard to bear, being on this
parts.note: something hard to bear is said to be on the heavy side

explanation.surface: A scientist was tough to put up with, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals a sound-alike: 'on the heavy side' means rather hard to bear. Oliver Heaviside was an English physicist who predicted the ionospheric layer named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: An English electrical engineer and mathematician who gave his name to a layer of the atmosphere.

clue.text: "Sweet Auburn! loveliest village of the —" (Goldsmith)

parts.note: the missing last word of the opening line of Oliver Goldsmith's poem The Deserted Village

explanation.surface: A line of eighteenth-century poetry with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Deserted Village (1770) opens 'Sweet Auburn! loveliest village of the plain'; fill the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's village lies on flat open ground, the word completing the line.

clue.text: Diner once troubled with such glands

indicators.note: troubled suggests the letters are stirred up and disordered

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer who was once unwell blames trouble with certain glands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges the nine letters of DINER ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ductless glands secreting hormones straight into the blood are described by this adjective.

clue.text: Pin back a climber

indicators.note: back tells us the word for pin is read from right to left

parts.note: to nail something is to pin it in place

explanation.surface: A mountaineer is told to fasten a rope behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' here is a plant, not a mountaineer; the A before it gives the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A woody tropical vine that clings its way up trees is a climbing plant.

clue.text: Committee gets a very generous cut

explanation.surface: A board of inquiry is awarded a lavish share.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is playful: a commission is a cut or percentage, and a royal one would be fit for a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A government inquiry body appointed by the Crown; also, jokingly, a princely percentage paid to an agent.

clue.text: Doctor describes it grammatically

explanation.surface: A physician explains how a word is used in grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'doctor' an animal is a euphemism for castrating it.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor a pet means to castrate it; in grammar the pronoun it belongs to the gender that is neither masculine nor feminine.

clue.text: Dundee MP, I worked out, is free

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scottish politician solved the problem and is now at liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges the nine letters of DUNDEE MP I.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhindered and unobstructed, at liberty to move.

clue.text: How tall is Mother Brown?

parts.note: alludes to the old music-hall song Knees Up Mother Brown, so her height is measured up to the knee

explanation.surface: A question about the height of a woman called Mother Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: Knees Up Mother Brown is a famous British pub and music-hall singalong song.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching up to the knee describes the height of something short, playing on the song title.

clue.text: A holiday with darling Cynthia

parts.note: honey is an endearment like darling
Cynthia is a poetic name for the moon goddess Artemis, born on Mount Cynthus

explanation.surface: Going away on a break with a beloved woman named Cynthia.
explanation.walkthrough: Cynthia is a classical name for the moon, from the moon goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The trip newlyweds take after the wedding is a kind of vacation.

clue.text: Build a frame

explanation.surface: An instruction to construct a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Build' looks like a verb but is the noun for body shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's bodily build or form; also the human frame.

clue.text: Records of monumental significance

parts.note: monumental here means carved on a monument, so these are inscriptions recorded on gravestones

explanation.surface: Historical documents of enormous importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monumental' looks like 'huge', but it literally means on a monument or tombstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Inscriptions on tombs record the dead, literally being words on a monument.

clue.text: Play Ted reviewed with expertise

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters are looked over again and rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic assessed a play by Ted with great skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges PLAY TED.
explanation.definitionFit: Done skilfully and proficiently, in an expert manner.

clue.text: Behind, like, with rent? That's bad

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as good as new'

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of rent have gone wrong and are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tenant complains that, as well as everything else, the rent is too high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link; 'That's bad' anagrams rent.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical term for at or towards the rear of a ship.

clue.text: After 8 it's easy going

parts.note: following the answer to 8 down this word forms an idiom for something straightforward

explanation.surface: Things get easier after eight o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 down is PLAIN; 'plain sailing' is an idiom for smooth progress. '8' looks like a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined to the previous word it forms a phrase meaning smooth, trouble-free progress.

clue.text: It's material, look, to make good

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A tailor says cloth and a fine appearance make clothes good.
explanation.walkthrough: REP (also repp) is a corded upholstery fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix or mend something is to restore it to good condition.

clue.text: Fast work by midwife or messenger

definitions.text: Fast work by midwife or messenger

parts.words: Fast work by midwife or messenger
parts.note: a quick birth delivered by a midwife, or a speedy parcel delivered by a courier

explanation.surface: Rapid service from either a midwife or a courier.
explanation.walkthrough: Both people 'deliver': the midwife a baby, the messenger a package.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick birth and a special rapid postal service are both speedy handovers.

clue.text: Obsolete decree or levy

parts.note: ex means former, no longer current
an act is a law or decree

explanation.surface: An old law or tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'levy' is the verb: to exact a tax is to demand it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact payment is to demand and collect it, as with a tax.

clue.text: Raise volume one quarter to show feeling

indicators.note: in a down clue raise means the word for volume is turned upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book or volume
E for east is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: Turning up the sound by a quarter to express emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' turns TOME upwards to EMOT, then E is added. 'volume' looks like loudness but is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To display emotion theatrically or exaggeratedly.

clue.text: Check accounts of what Salisbury declared in Army return

indicators.note: in tells us the declaration goes inside the army abbreviation
return means the army abbreviation is turned back to front

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
UDI, the Unilateral Declaration of Independence, was announced in 1965 by Rhodesia's government in its capital Salisbury

explanation.surface: An inspection of the books concerning a political declaration made on a soldier's return.
explanation.walkthrough: Salisbury here is the old name of Harare, capital of Rhodesia, not the English city or the Victorian prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of an organisation's financial records.

clue.text: Crooked bell-ringer nominated for Low Sunday

explanation.surface: A dishonest campanologist is put up for an award on a church feast day.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hugo's novel the hunchback is named after the Sunday after Easter, when he was found; that day's Latin introit begins 'Quasi modo'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hunched ringer of Notre-Dame in Victor Hugo's novel; also the Latin-derived name for the first Sunday after Easter.

clue.text: Nominally Roosevelt's plaything

parts.note: a toy named after the American president known by the nickname Teddy

explanation.surface: A toy that belonged to a US president in name only.
explanation.walkthrough: The stuffed toy was named after President Theodore 'Teddy' Roosevelt after he refused to shoot a bear cub.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuddly stuffed toy takes its name from the president's nickname.

clue.text: New angle on what Ruth offered to do

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of angle

explanation.surface: A fresh perspective on what a woman named Ruth proposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges ANGLE. In the Bible, Ruth asked to gather leftover grain in the fields of Boaz.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth gathered stray ears of barley after the reapers, the act of collecting leftovers.
